summary: Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John Niemeyer Findlay. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007).

Joseph Ratzinger was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Munich (~1947–1951) and Ducal Georgianum (1949–1951). His academic posts included Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen (~1966–1969), and Regensburg (~1969–1977).

Joseph Rock was active in linguistics, sinology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), the University of Hawaiʻi (1908; 1911–1920 as curator and botanist), the USDA (~1920–1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).
Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. A Jesuit missionary with the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773, he also served as Rector of the Jesuit High School of Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later succeeding him at INALCO (1838). He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Société Asiatique.

Linguist Joseph Vendryes studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and under Antoine Meillet (~1898–1901). He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1904–1946) and the University of Paris (~1907–1946).
Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He pursued his studies under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and later held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).

Joshua Ereshefsky is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at McMaster University as a PhD candidate in religious studies under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2026).

Joshua Marshman was a scholar of sinology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and went on to found Serampore College in 1818.

Linguist Joshua T. Katz studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (~2022).
Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

Philosopher Josiah Royce studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) before his long tenure on the faculty at Harvard University (1882–1916).

Jost Gippert specializes in linguistics, computational linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Marburg (~1974–1975), he held posts at several universities, notably directing the Institute for Empirical Linguistics at Goethe University Frankfurt (1994–2022).

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and Wisconsin under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and became Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Khur-Yearn earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Göttingen, Hamburg (under Lambert Schmithausen), and Munich (under Jens-Uwe Hartmann). She held posts at Munich (2017–2021) and became Professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Cecile Brennan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. Brennan earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard A. Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Goshen College (~1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1978–1984), later serving as Professor Emerita at Emory University (~1992).
